gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Playful and softly pinched, Irish Grover stands up its heavy lowercase while Noto Sans Tirhuta trails behind in a plain sans with a dominant x-height. And over a long page, those cut-back terminals leave generous gaps that keep the text moving.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-vai: Fun and a little wobbly, Irish Grover pinches slightly wherever its curves meet a stem, giving each word a chunky, hand-shaped look. Then Noto Sans Vai settles in as a sans-serif body, and a longer passage reads as solid blocks with room around every curve end.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Tall, sturdy lowercase with just a touch of stroke modulation gives Irish Grover its character, while Noto Sans Vithkuqi stays out of its way. Long stretches in that plain sans feel clean, with barely a step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-warang-cit: Chunky, friendly and hand-shaped, with comfortable thick and thin strokes. Irish Grover's best quality is how readily it hands off to Noto Sans Warang Citi, whose low-contrast words form solid blocks with wide channels leading into each counter.
gen-irish-grover-gf-orienta: Orienta is modern and level-headed, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open and little height difference between cases. Orienta carries a longer stretch of text without strain, while Irish Grover above it leans on gently pressed diagonals and sturdy, tall-standing words.
gen-irish-grover-gf-oxygen: Irish Grover leads with fun, organic letters whose light stroke modulation only shows when you look closely. But Oxygen follows in a plain sans where the curves never close back on themselves, so a longer passage runs smoothly with lowercase nearly matching the capitals.
gen-irish-grover-gf-preahvihear: Preahvihear reads wide open, with mouths like a pried oyster shell and a lofty x-height. Preahvihear against Irish Grover is the whole appeal: a sturdy, fun heading whose thins never turn spindly, over a sans that stays light and spacious.
gen-irish-grover-gf-questrial: Fun and organic, Irish Grover has curves that lighten mildly toward their ends, which gives each heading some softness. And Questrial answers underneath as a sans-serif, its strokes like drawn with a fixed pen, flat and stencil-cut in a tall band of letters.
gen-irish-grover-gf-radio-canada: Sturdy, rounded and slightly cheeky, Irish Grover brings moderate contrast to its headings. But Radio Canada does the quieter work as a sans-serif, with a steady line, no pressure variation and clear openings at the end of every curve.
gen-irish-grover-gf-saira: Saira is neat and clean, with a visible gap in each s and rounded letters stretching toward the top line. Irish Grover does its best work with modest, readable weight shifts across every curve, whereas Saira keeps the sans-serif text low in contrast and tidy.
